title: Elijah and the Still Small Voice

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Elijah had just seen God answer with fire on Mount Carmel. It was the greatest victory of his life. But the queen was not moved by it at all.

verses.text: And Ahab told Jezebel all that Elijah had done, and withal how he had slain all the prophets with the sword.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The same prophet who stood up to hundreds of false prophets now sat alone under a tree and asked to die. He was worn out, afraid, and sure he had failed.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: If you have ever been that tired, you are not the first. And notice what God did next. He did not scold Elijah. He did not give him a speech.

verses.text: And as he lay and slept under a juniper tree, behold, then an angel touched him, and said unto him, Arise and eat.

verses.text: And the angel of the LORD came again the second time, and touched him, and said, Arise and eat; because the journey is too great for thee.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Sleep, and warm bread, and water, and a gentle touch. Twice. God knew the journey was too much for him, and he took care of his body before anything else.

verses.text: And he arose, and did eat and drink, and went in the strength of that meat forty days and forty nights unto Horeb the mount of God.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Elijah poured it all out. He had done everything he could, and now he felt like the only one left.

verses.text: And he said, Go forth, and stand upon the mount before the LORD. blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Wind that broke the rocks. An earthquake. A fire. All of it loud and frightening, and God was in none of it. Then, after all the noise, there was a still small voice.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: God did not leave Elijah sitting in the cave. He gave him rest, then he spoke to him quietly, then he gave him something to do. Soon after, God told him he was not alone after all. There were still seven thousand in Israel who had not turned away.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Sometimes we look for God in the wind and the fire. Sometimes he comes in a quiet voice, after the noise has passed. And sometimes the first thing he gives a weary person is a meal and a good night's sleep. If tonight feels like Elijah's tree, you do not have to sit under it alone. Tell someone who loves you.

first_reader.note: Written by Claude in the landing session, then Claude's pastor and cultural read.

pastor.note: Faithful to 1 Kings 19:1-15 (the 7,000 is v18); Elijah's wish to die told honestly and gently; God's care is rest, food and a quiet word; the close points a weary listener to a person who loves her, with no promise of an outcome. A deacon board would read it aloud.

cultural.note: Tender, not preachy; despair is not shamed.
